GIN's 0.2% accuracy and approximately zero macro-F1 on HSG-topology could reflect optimization failure. The full dataset, three-band subset, and temporal collection receive no benchmark evaluation.

Random stratified splits of the coefficient grid leave duplication and generalization unresolved. For the included p=q=2 one-band family, simultaneously negating both free coefficients preserves the spectrum through z -> -z. No audit establishes whether equivalent spectra cross splits. Grouping spectral equivalents and holding out parameter regions would help distinguish interpolation or memorization from broader generalization.

The advertised million-fold speedup and 20–40-fold memory improvement lack a reproducible comparative benchmark: absolute timings, matched hardware, workloads, numerical accuracy, and component ablations are absent. Footnote 6 restricts the comparison to spectral-potential computation, while the manuscript repeatedly promotes the broader pipeline using these figures.

The universal-fingerprint claim exceeds the argument in Appendix E. A nonunique Toeplitz factorization provides an association with graphs, but an unordered multiset also discards multiplication order; a canonical or discriminative matrix representation does not follow. No downstream experiment establishes the utility of this construction, and the broader scientific-discovery claims remain prospective.
